goto.does: open a full URL on a stand host named in config environments[]; the first goto of the file names the stand of the session

fill.does: type the text into the field; never a credential - an account goes in with `fill-account`

fill-account.does: type the account's name (user) or password (secret) into the field; the actor is a form of `--as` (default, a role, env:USER_KEY/SECRET_KEY, created:<name>) and the value is read by code, never written in the steps file; the screen is not saved from the first such step until the page leaves the sign-in address

type.does: focus the field once, then key the text one character at a time with the pause between characters, and record the field's value and whether it still has focus after each character, then once more after `settle_ms`; use it when a field's value goes to the server or redraws the page (`fill` sets the whole value at once and hides a lost character or a lost focus); a text longer than max_chars is `fill`

press.does: focus the field and press one key from `keys` (or one printable character); records the field's value and its focus, and whether it had focus before the step

paste.does: focus the field and insert the text at once (an `input` event, not a `paste` event); records the field's value and its focus

fail_request.does: from now on every browser request of the page that matches the glob gets the status (an empty JSON body) or is dropped as timed out; it does not reach the stand; a glob with a host must name a stand host; a request sent by the page's server is not seen

restore_request.does: stop failing the requests of the glob; the record of what was failed stays for the session

drag.does: press on the element, move the mouse by dx, dy pixels (whole numbers), release

wait.does: a whole number is milliseconds; anything else waits for the selector to appear

read.does: store the value (text by default) in a log file and in the step line; this is how a viewport transform or a status text is read; an attribute the element lacks reads as read_absent_marker, an empty one as nothing; state= is true or false for one of read_states

capture.does: take a screenshot now; the label names the file and is what the capture proves: `capture post_action completion` is the one line that proves the completion condition was reached

words.source_factory_default: the factory's default recipe, which this project never confirmed
words.not_known_line: login by code: this project's sign-in is not an HTTP request the factory knows (environment.access.kind {kind}); nothing was sent
words.not_known_door: record manual_capture.login.http in config.json (path and token_field), or null if this kind of capture needs no login; a screen case signs in with fill-account steps
words.default_unconfirmed: login by code at {url} did not give a token ({status}). The address is the factory's default recipe, which this project never confirmed, so the stand has not judged the account: record manual_capture.login.http in config.json (path and token_field), or record the sign-in as environment.access of kind local_login with its url; say so in your findings
words.none_said: environment.access.kind is none: no login by code

manual_capture.py ui.input: --task-root <T> --case <id> --steps-file <file> [--as <account>] [--session <actor>] [--attempt a<n>]: --session keeps that actor's browser profile between calls (calls of one --profile join one open attempt; leave --as out; the stand probe of gate A must have proved the sign-in), and `manual_capture.py session close --task-root <T> --case <id> [--attempt a<n>]` deletes the profiles - run it before `build`, which refuses a live profile. One step per line from the closed list in references/manual-capture-steps.json - goto <url>, click <selector>, fill <selector> <text>, fill-account <selector> <actor> user|secret, drag <selector> dx dy, wait <ms>|<selector>, read <selector> [attr=<name>|style=<prop>|text], capture <pre_action|post_action|supporting> [label]. The file holds at least one goto (the first goto names the session's stand), and every goto must be on a configured stand; `capture post_action completion` proves the completion condition; never type a credential in a step - the code signs in (`--as` names the account), or `fill-account` types the account the factory resolves (a steps file with `fill-account` makes no code login, so leave `--as` out).
manual_capture.py ui.verify: the printed JSON lists every capture with its phase and every step with its outcome; exit 0 means every step ran, 1 a step failed or timed out, 3 the stand could not be identified, or the login by code did not land (`do_not_retry`, owner `user`: the account was refused - make no further capture of any kind in this block, put the case in env_blocked[] with the printed `login by code: ...` line and halt the block, never `build`; owner `factory`: the recipe did not fit the page - sign in ONCE through `fill-account` steps in a new attempt, then the same halt if that fails).

manual_capture.py http.input: --task-root <T> --case <id> --method GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD|OPTIONS --url <url on a configured stand> [--body-file <file>] [--header "Name: value"]... [--state-url <url>] [--phase pre_action|post_action|supporting] [--proves <word>]... [--as <account>] [--session <actor>: the request carries that session's cookies only in the same --profile's open attempt; without --profile it opens its own attempt and signs in again] [--attempt a<n>]. Without --phase the call is a post_action; `--proves completion` marks the completion condition reached; --state-url also saves a GET of that URL as the state; never put a credential in a header - the code signs in (`--as` names the account); to create a user, put `{generated_username}` and `{generated_password}` in the --body-file (only there): the factory fills them in and keeps the password out of every output.
manual_capture.py http.verify: the printed JSON lists the saved request_response (and state) with phase and hash; exit 0 means the call was answered, 1 it timed out, 3 the stand could not be identified (the case is env_blocked, no record).
